headline: Bitcoin fell for a third straight day to its lowest since early July, the US Senate voted to ban prediction bets on death and war while Coinbase plans its own prediction contracts, and Anthropic's stock tokens slid further than the real shares.

stories.title: Bitcoin falls for a third straight day to its lowest since early July as leveraged bets are wiped out
stories.summary: Bitcoin slipped to nearly $61,200 on Friday, a little below Thursday's low, before bouncing back above $61,700, as the selloff in tech stocks spread through Asia. More than $700 million of leveraged bets were forced shut in a day, most of them bets on prices rising. When borrowed-money traders and big funds pull out together, prices can fall faster than the news alone would suggest.
points: South Korea's Kospi fell more than 5% and US tech futures were down more than 1% as bitcoin fell, per CoinDesk (11:42 UTC).
$718.6 million of crypto bets were liquidated in 24 hours, 86.2% of them from traders betting on a rise, per CoinDesk.
US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $582.19 million on 19 Nov, including $541.08 million from BlackRock's IBIT, per Bloomingbit; CoinDesk says it was IBIT's largest single-day outflow since launch.
Open interest across crypto futures fell 2.5% to $109.9 billion, and bitcoin funding rates turned broadly negative, meaning more traders are now paying to bet on a fall, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin is down more than 20% from about $81,000 at the start of November, per U.Today.

stories.title: Senate votes to ban prediction bets on death and war as Coinbase plans its own prediction contracts
stories.summary: The US Senate passed the Death Bets Act on Thursday, which would ban prediction-market contracts on death, terrorism, assassination and war; it now goes to the House. Separately, Coinbase is aiming to list its own US prediction contracts in the first half of 2027, relying less on its partner Kalshi. Prediction markets are becoming a mainstream product on US crypto apps, and Washington is starting to set limits on what people can bet on.
points: The bill, S.4035, was sponsored by Sen. Schiff and co-sponsored by Sen. Curtis, and would amend the Commodity Exchange Act, per The Block.
More than a dozen states have taken action against Kalshi, and the CFTC and Justice Department have sued Utah, Arkansas and Louisiana, per The Block.
Coinbase's Kalshi partnership brought in more than $200 million of annualized net revenue in the third quarter, per CoinDesk, citing a Bloomberg report.
Average daily prediction-market traders on Coinbase rose more than 60% from the prior quarter, and more than half of third-quarter prediction trades were not on sports, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Anthropic shares point lower before Friday's open, and crypto token versions fall much further
stories.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed its first Nasdaq day at $97.17. Before Friday's US open the shares were down about 5% to around $92, while a crypto token that tracks the stock fell 21%. A token or contract that follows a stock is not the same as owning the stock, and it can move very differently.
points: The IPO raised about $81.3 billion, or $107.3 billion including a $26 billion private placement, per CoinDesk.
PreStocks' ANT token fell 21% to $69.48, per CoinDesk.
Hyperliquid's ANT perpetual contract traded in the low $90s, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Ether funds lose money for a fifth day
briefs.summary: US spot ether funds lost a net $131 million on 19 Nov, a fifth straight day of outflows; bitcoin and ether funds together lost $713 million, per KuCoin News.

briefs.title: Sky's stUSDS savers still stuck
briefs.summary: Sky raised the stUSDS deposit rate to 24.74%, but its app still showed no liquidity for withdrawals; one borrower repaid about 414,000 USDS, per The Defiant.

briefs.title: Wrapped Monero token crashes 99%
briefs.summary: Wagyu's XMR1 token fell from about $488 to about $1 in roughly 30 minutes after a wallet funded by the issuer's address sold about $13.5 million; real Monero was not affected, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Ethereum's next upgrade slips to 2027
briefs.summary: The Glamsterdam upgrade moves from December to mid-January 2027 at the earliest while developers fix apps that could break, per CoinCentral.

briefs.title: MoonPay applies for a US bank charter
briefs.summary: MoonPay applied to the OCC for a national trust bank charter covering custody and stablecoin issuance, per The Block.

briefs.title: CFTC chair on Hyperliquid and US users
briefs.summary: CFTC Chair Selig said on-chain venues like Hyperliquid can serve US retail only by registering as an exchange or partnering with one, per The Block.

briefs.title: Crypto market-structure bill stalls
briefs.summary: Rep. French Hill and Sen. Moreno expect little progress on the Clarity Act before the new Congress, per The Block.
